title: Sentinel Data Connectors and Event Collection

questions.sub_skill: Configure and use Microsoft data connectors for Azure resources
questions.prompt: You enable the Microsoft Defender XDR connector and leave the individual Defender product connectors enabled. What happens?
options: Sentinel deduplicates automatically; there is no effect
The same events are ingested twice, billed twice, and every count in every query you write afterwards is wrong
The XDR connector takes precedence and the product connectors become inert
Ingestion fails with a schema conflict
questions.explanation: The unified connector supersedes the individual ones. Leaving both on is the most common avoidable Sentinel cost, and the duplicate rows quietly corrupt every aggregation.

questions.sub_skill: Implement and configure syslog and Common Event Format (CEF) event collections
questions.prompt: A firewall vendor asks how to send logs to Sentinel. Describe the architecture and the destination table.
options: Install the Azure Monitor Agent on the appliance; events land in Syslog
Send syslog to a Linux forwarder running the Azure Monitor Agent, configured by the CEF via AMA connector; structured events land in CommonSecurityLog
Use a data collection endpoint and the Logs Ingestion API; events land in a custom table
Enable diagnostic settings on the appliance; events land in AzureDiagnostics
questions.explanation: Appliances do not run agents, so the forwarder pattern is mandatory rather than stylistic. CEF is a structured key-value extension of syslog, which is why it lands parsed in CommonSecurityLog rather than as raw text in Syslog.

questions.sub_skill: Implement and configure collection of Windows Security events by using data collection rules, including Windows Event Forwarding (WEF)
questions.prompt: A requirement says to collect only specific Windows event IDs, and nothing else. Which option?
options: The Minimal predefined event set
A custom XPath query in the Windows Security Events data collection rule
A KQL transformation on the DCR
The Common predefined event set with an exclusion list
questions.explanation: All events, Common and Minimal are the predefined sets. 'Collect only these event IDs' is an XPath question. A transformation reshapes data after collection is defined; XPath decides what is collected at all.

questions.sub_skill: Implement and configure collection of Windows Security events by using data collection rules, including Windows Event Forwarding (WEF)
questions.prompt: Your analytics rule for suspicious logons has returned nothing for three weeks. The rule is enabled and its query is correct. What would you check on the collection side?
options: Whether an XPath filter or predefined event set removed the event IDs the rule queries
Whether both the Security log connector and WEF collection are enabled on the same collector
Whether the daily cap has been dropping data
Whether the workspace region matches the rule
questions.explanation: Two collection-side causes produce silence. A filter chosen to save money can remove the exact event IDs a detection depends on, and a daily cap drops data once reached. Enabling both the Security log connector and WEF would produce duplicates, not silence.

questions.sub_skill: Create custom log tables in the workspace to store ingested data
questions.prompt: An application has no connector. You must retain twelve months of its verbose logs for compliance and run detections against a small subset. Describe the design.
options: One custom table on the Analytics plan, with twelve-month interactive retention
A custom table plus a DCR with a data collection endpoint; detection-relevant data on the Analytics plan, verbose telemetry on a cheaper tier, with long-term retention for the rest
Ingest everything to Syslog via a forwarder and filter at query time
Store the logs in a storage account and query them with a search job
questions.explanation: Custom tables are DCR-based and need a data collection endpoint — ingestion fails quietly without one. Everything on the Analytics plan because it is the default is the most common cost mistake after over-collection.

questions.sub_skill: Create custom log tables in the workspace to store ingested data
questions.prompt: What does a KQL transformation in a data collection rule do, and what is the risk?
options: It filters at query time, so nothing is lost and cost is unchanged
It reshapes data before it is stored, so you pay for what you keep — and what it drops is gone, not hidden
It converts custom tables to the Analytics plan automatically
It applies only to Windows Security events
questions.explanation: Transformations drop columns, filter rows and normalise fields at ingestion. That is the cost lever, and it carries the same asymmetry as every other collection decision: a transformation written and never reviewed removes a field a future detection needs, invisibly.
